title: Model Compatibility Signal Orchestration and Monitoring
creator: Sofia Reynolds
description: Establish a lightweight, automated pipeline that ingests external model-landscape signals (new model releases, breaking API changes, license shifts, quantization/precision variants, published performance regressions) and surfaces prioritized compatibility risks and remediation playbooks inside Redwood’s product tooling and PM/Eng workflows.
background: We currently rely on manual scouting and ad-hoc alerts from research & comms. As the open-model ecosystem accelerates, manual triage is a scaling bottleneck and increases time-to-detect for critical compatibility issues affecting Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This work combines competitive monitoring with operational guardrails (alerts, runbooks, dashboards) so teams can respond faster to model churn and deprecation signals.
goals: Automate ingestion of 3 primary external feeds: GitHub model-repo releases (tags/PRs), vendor announcements (RSS/webhook), and benchmark/perf feeds (internal eval runner output)
Produce a ranked compatibility-risk scoreboard (breaking API, tokenizer changes, quant/precision mismatch, license) with confidence scoring
Integrate signal alerts into Console (incidents/notes) and Slack channel + create templated remediation runbooks
Reduce time-to-detect compatibility breaks from days to <6 hours and reduce manual triage overhead by ~60% for PM/Eng teams
success_metrics: Median time from external release -> first Signal detection: <6 hours
% of high-confidence breaking signals auto-tagged and assigned: >= 80%
Reduction in manual triage hours per week across PM/Eng: 60%
Number of prevented customer-facing regressions attributed to early detection: >= 3 in first quarter post-launch
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests model release events from at least one GitHub org, the vendor announcement feed, and the internal eval runner
Console shows a sortable compatibility scoreboard filtered by region, deployment type, and model family
Slack alerts are sent to #pm-model-watch with a link to a Console signal page and an auto-suggested remediation template
Playbook templates exist for four common signal types: API change, tokenizer/vocab mismatch, quantization/precision incompatibility, and license change
A documented runbook exists for false-positive handling and signal tuning
tasks: Define signal taxonomy and confidence model (PM + Research)
Prototype ingestion lambda (ENG) for GitHub + RSS webhook receivers
Create minimal scoreboard schema and Console UI wireframes (Design + PM)
Implement Slack integration and templated assignment rules (Eng)
Build eval hooks to surface regressions from internal benchmark runner
Author remediation playbooks and add to Confluence
Run a 2-week field trial with three internal product teams and capture feedback
updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Research, Eng infra, Console UX. Agreed scope: MVP will cover tokenizer, API contract, and license signals for top-10 models by usage.
2025-02-20: PM/Research draft taxonomy v0.1 posted to Confluence (link below). Decided to prioritize high-confidence heuristic rules before ML-based signal fusion.
2025-02-28: Eng prototype ingestor (GitHub releases + vendor RSS) available behind feature flag; initial false-positive rate measured at ~30% on synthetic replay dataset.
2025-03-04: Design delivered wireframe for scoreboard and signal detail page. UX review requested (Design: Mark Chen).
2025-03-04: Slack alert format reviewed with SRE for rate limits and escalation semantics.
decisions: MVP will use deterministic heuristics (regex and manifest diffs) rather than ML fusion to keep iteration fast
Signal priority scoring will be a linear combination of (impact_estimate, confidence, customer_exposure) with weights tunable in Console
Do not auto-escalate to customer-facing incidents in MVP; only create internal tickets and playbook suggestions
Keep Private/VPC customers out of automated ingest for sensitive repos until KMS/entitlements gating is implemented
risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives create noise — tradeoff: favor higher precision for P1 signals and accept lower recall in MVP
Cost of continuous evals — mitigation: sample releases for full evals and run lightweight heuristics for everything else
Surface-level signals may not reflect semantic regressions — dependent on Research to define targeted evals for high-risk changes
Potential legal/OSS license edge cases — coordinate with Legal before auto-tagging commercial risk
next_steps: Finalize taxonomy and rule set (PM + Research) by 2025-03-10
Reduce prototype false-positive rate to <15% by iterating heuristics (Eng) by 2025-03-24
Deploy MVP scoreboard to staging Console and enable Slack alerts for internal alpha group by 2025-04-01
Schedule 2-week field trial and collect structured feedback using the trial feedback template
